name: utf16_urls
description: String candidates for URLs, file: and Visited: entries and 192.168.x.x addresses in a file; not a browser parser. ascii: http:// or https:// and at least six URL characters, to the first byte that is not one, with no length cut off. utf16le: a run of at least eight UTF-16LE characters that contains http, file:, visited: or 192.168; a run begins at a printable ASCII character and goes on through printable ASCII, Latin-1 and the letters of Latin Extended, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic, Indic and Thai (so https://örnek.test/ is one candidate; CJK is not read, its code units are ASCII letter pairs); a NUL, a control character or a surrogate ends it. Every occurrence is kept with its byte offset and encoding (the same text twice is two candidates); a groups view lists each distinct text once with its count and first offset (bounded by max_distinct, and says when it stopped growing). The file is read in windows with a carry, never whole, so a match that straddles a window is found once; a run longer than the carry is returned in adjacent pieces (continued: true on all but the last) so no character is lost. A string does not say it was visited, typed, downloaded or opened, or by whom. SENSITIVE: a URL can carry a session token or a password in its query string, fragment or user-info; the values are found by parameter name and by user-info (a query-string or fragment parameter whose name says token, secret, password, key, session, signature and the like, and the password of the user-info), and the text of every candidate is returned with those values replaced by a marker holding only their length; a token under another parameter name, or in a path, is printed with the rest (measured on generated canaries: every one of the 20 printed whole in a path and under an unlisted name, 0 under a listed name or in user-info), url_secrets_withheld says how many, of what kind and at which offset, and contains is matched against the text as returned. write_url_secrets: true writes the whole text to a 0600 file under $OUT, in a job run with secret_output: true only. A secret in a path or in free text is not found. An unreadable file is a JSON failure. The tool has its own clock (54 s of the manifest's 60): when it runs out the work stops, the pages written so far are placed and named, and the answer is partial with a status_basis that says where it stopped and how many bytes were scanned whole; every answer carries status and status_basis (complete only for an input read to its end), a wrong-type argument is refused as JSON (status failed), and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file. A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. A file name that is not UTF-8 is answered (the path is shown with its bytes escaped).

contains.description: Optional substring filter (case-insensitive) on the candidate text; the candidates it leaves out are counted under filtered_out_by_contains

limit.description: Candidates and groups shown inline, each (default 200, 1 to 10000, an inline page size); every one is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

chunk.description: Bytes read per window (default 8 MiB, from 131072 to 33554432): a window costs about four times its size in memory

max_distinct.description: Distinct texts the groups view tracks (default 100000, at most 1000000); past it the view stops growing and groups_complete is false (the status is partial), while every occurrence is still a candidate

write_url_secrets.description: Write the whole text of every URL whose secrets were withheld, with the secret value, to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced). Secret output: refused as JSON, before anything is created, unless the job runs with secret_output (the manifest declares it for this parameter); default false
